Compal Electronics.why: Notebook ODM ramping an AI server business: AI servers were about 70% of server revenue in 1H26, most of it B300 systems built at L10 in Taipei, with 2027 server revenue guided at 30%-40% of company revenue.
Compal Electronics.evidence: Compal Electronics Q2 FY2026 (08-13-2026), CEO Tony Bonadero: "Most of that revenue is from B300, and most of that being L10 manufactured here in Taipei today."
Compal Electronics.approved: user pre-approved 2026-09-28 for waitlist group weak_evidence (enrich_waitlist.json, group weak_evidence)

players.product: AI server ODM: NVIDIA B300 systems built mostly at L10 rack level in Taipei, with board assembly through L6 / L10 / L11 full-rack integration at new Taiwan and Texas sites

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 revenue TWD 238.3 billion, up 32% year over year; gross margin 4.6%, hit by rising component costs, particularly memory; operating profit TWD 2.8 billion (+8% QoQ, +9% YoY); net profit TWD 3.1 billion (+59% QoQ), EPS TWD 0.73; first-half net profit TWD 5.1 billion (+91% YoY).
quarterly_data.figure: revenue TWD 238.3 billion (+32% YoY); gross margin 4.6%; net profit TWD 3.1 billion (+59% QoQ)

quarterly_data.signal: Non-PC revenue TWD 82 billion (+15% QoQ, +52% YoY), about 35% of revenue (up about 5 percentage points YoY), driven mainly by the AI server ramp; FY2026 non-PC mix targeted to approach 40%. Notebook revenue TWD 156 billion (+20% QoQ, +23% YoY); notebook shipments +5% QoQ and -13% YoY on component supply constraints and price increases; FY2026 PC shipments expected to decline at a mid-teens rate; IR: around 50% of first-half shipments and about 60% of revenue were AI PC related.
quarterly_data.figure: non-PC revenue TWD 82 billion (+52% YoY); notebook revenue TWD 156 billion

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: Q1 2026 server revenue already equaled all of FY 2025; AI servers ramped to 70%-80% of server revenue in 2Q 2026. IR: servers were around 5% of total revenue in Q1 and high single digit in Q2, on track for the 10% target for 2026; about 70% of first-half AI server revenue is already L10. CEO: most of that revenue is from B300, mostly L10 manufactured in Taipei; neoclouds provided much of the Q2 growth, with AI cloud wins across Europe, Asia and the U.S.; next year should bring a mix of neoclouds, tier 1 hyperscalers and at least one large enterprise.
quarterly_data.figure: AI servers 70%-80% of server revenue in 2Q 2026; servers high single digit of revenue; 10% target for 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Guidance: Q3 server revenue expected to increase by high double digits quarter over quarter, PC units flat, smart device revenue to decline; CEO: 4Q AI server momentum to remain healthy. CEO confirmed as guidance that 30%-40% of Compal's revenue in 2027 will come from the server business, the vast majority from AI servers, taking PCs below 50% of revenue. IR: OpEx targeted at single-digit growth year over year.
quarterly_data.figure: 2027 server revenue 30%-40% of company revenue; Q3 server revenue +high double digits QoQ

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: larger rack manufacturing will start in the Q1 timeframe of 2027; a new tier 1 neocloud and a large U.S. enterprise customer are being prepared in the second half of 2026 and will ramp in very early Q1 2027, expanding from B300 into full rack solutions.

IR: 2026 CapEx guidance TWD 18 billion; about TWD 9 billion spent in the first half, of which TWD 6 billion to TWD 7 billion was server related (Daxi in Taiwan, Vinh Phuc SMT lines, Texas in the U.S., from SMT to L10/L11); this year and next will be capacity expansion years. CEO: two new sites in Taiwan and the United States and expanded capacity across four countries, ramping by the end of 2026; the Taiwan site is an NPI facility for AI server and cooling manufacturing with full rack level integration; the U.S. site covers board assembly through full rack L6, L10, L11.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 CapEx TWD 18 billion; TWD 6 billion to TWD 7 billion server CapEx in the first half

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: B300 demand is very strong through this year; as the Vera CPU comes in it will start to take over, and that transition will happen pretty quickly, with little overlap between generations.

IR: first-half server gross margin was higher than the corporate average, with margins varying by customer and project as L6 moves to L10; CEO: server pricing is not percentage-based, GPU silicon providers take a huge portion of the BOM in large rack systems, and the company runs a buy-sell model with no consignment customer today.

CEO: component supply must be secured carefully (PCB, wiring, connectors); Q2 had a dip in May because parts could not be obtained, then a very strong June; 2027 may bring more memory inflation and in many cases parts simply cannot be obtained; the PC industry faces a fundamental margin reset as component costs rise faster than the market will tolerate price increases.
